title: Ruben Hassid on growing on LinkedIn with AI: taste, volume, and one mission
summary: Ruben explains how he grew to 400K+ LinkedIn followers and built EasyGen, a bootstrapped post generator. AI rewards taste and volume (generate many, curate the best), not one-shot prompts. His LinkedIn playbook: one tight problem, many solutions, double down on winners, and engage.

principles.text: AI replaces mediocrity, not people. Taste, experience and high standards, multiplied by volume, are the edge.
principles.quote: mediocrity is going to be replaced very fast it's already happening if most of your job is writing OK articles you're going to be replaced really fast

principles.text: Never one-shot AI output. Generate many variations, then use your taste to select and patchwork the best parts.
principles.quote: by the time you try to find a topic I wrote and generated 30 posts on the same topic more or less

principles.text: Use AI to be greater, not lazier: do more and better work instead of finishing the day after one quick generation.
principles.quote: I'm using AI to be greater not to be lazier the idea is I can do more

principles.text: Start LinkedIn with one tight problem (your mission), then cover it with many solutions and repeat yourself often.
principles.quote: one problem to solve and the the the simpler the problem the easier for you um and then many solutions

principles.text: Run a 30-day test of formats and angles, then double down on the best five winners; don't retry the losers.
principles.quote: you analyze the best five and the worst five and you do the best five 30 times the next months

principles.text: Engagement matters as much as posting, especially early. You can't want a community and never talk to anyone in it.
principles.quote: engaging it's just as important it's not way more important in the beginning
